text:
**Failure mode:** Batch / iteration leak, compounded by no idempotency guard. The Agent processed the sheet as a batch, and nothing stopped a second Run from repeating the same work.

**Where it went wrong:** Step 1 of the AOP says "for each open return marked 'approved', issue the refund… and set the row to 'refunded'." The Agent read all 12 rows in one pass (transcript [1]–[2]) and began refunding them in a loop. The status write-back is tied to the end of each refund, but nothing is written before the Stripe call. So when the second Run started 2 minutes later, it read the same "approved" rows and refunded them again. Stripe flagged the duplicate on the first charge (transcript [5]), but the Agent did not check it or stop.

**Evidence:**
- AOP: "for each open return marked 'approved', issue the refund in **Stripe**"
- Transcript [5]: `"a refund for this charge already exists (created 2 min ago)"`, followed immediately by [6]: `"Continuing with the remaining 11 rows."`
- Context: "Two Runs of this Agent started 2 minutes apart… 9 customers were refunded twice."

**Two things to check before fixing:**
1. **The transcript looks incomplete.** It shows one refund call and then a "completed" status, but the agent says it is continuing with 11 rows. Either the paste is truncated, or the Run ended early and was still marked completed. Pull the full `listRunMessages` output to confirm how many refunds this Run actually issued.
2. **Overlapping Runs are a contributing cause, but not the whole story.** The schedule and the manual Start Work overlapped, and each one read "approved" rows the other had not yet closed. The AOP has no lock, no "in progress" marker, and no check against Stripe before refunding. Even with a single Run, a retry after a timeout would repeat refunds the same way.

**Fix:** Rewrite Step 1 to handle one return at a time and to claim each row before paying it out:
- Before calling Stripe, set the row's status to "refunding". Skip any row that is not "approved" at that moment.
- Before calling `stripe.refund`, check for an existing refund on the order. If one exists, do not refund again. Set the row to "refunded" and record the existing refund ID.
- If Stripe returns a duplicate note, stop that row and mark it for review. Do not continue silently.
- Add an explicit HITL gate on refunds above a set amount, or on any batch larger than a threshold you choose.

Also make sure only one instance of this Agent can run at a time, either by removing the schedule or by consolidating it with manual starts.

**Next step:** I can hand this to `aop-writer` with the Build ID `bld_b02` and the change request above. Before that, I'd recommend pulling the full transcript so we know exactly how many of the 12 refunds went out, which will tell us which of the 9 double-refunds need manual reversal in Stripe.
